title: Support-sensitive public campaign financing
text:
### Support-sensitive public campaign financing

**Governing question:** Whether competing parties must receive equal public presidential-campaign subsidies.

**Current rule:** The Constitution does not require equal subsidies merely because parties compete or qualify for public financing. A formula tied to prior electoral support and inability to match larger parties’ resources do not alone establish the materially different practical suppression or discriminatory administration needed for a distinct constitutional challenge. Inability to close that subsidy gap under an individual-candidate contribution limit does not alone establish an impairment different from the rejected parity claim; it supplies no permanent dollar safe harbor. Concrete exclusionary administration, viewpoint favoritism and materially different cumulative or prohibitory burdens require their own analysis. A party need not disappear or cease fielding candidates before challenging a substantially suppressive application.

**Authority by component:**

- National Committee of the Reform Party v. Democratic National Committee — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, “I. Demonstrated electoral support does not create a duty to equalize subsidies”, 1999-03-17; Thomas Parts I–III, all nine Justices. Part I supplies subsidy treatment; Part II, “The actual contribution-limit argument requires its own narrow answer”, supplies the separate contribution-gap boundary.

**Present operation effective:** Reform Party, March 17, 1999.

title: Special statutory tribunals for election-financing challenges
text:
### Special statutory tribunals for election-financing challenges

**Governing question:** When a constitutional election-financing claim must enter FECA’s or the Fund Act’s special statutory tribunal.

**Current rule:** A claim lacking Article III standing or presenting a constitutional theory plainly foreclosed by controlling law may be rejected before invoking the extraordinary statutory tribunal. A live substantial constitutional question cannot be bypassed because the court expects it to fail. A substantial qualifying FECA constitutional question brought by an authorized plaintiff follows §437h to the court of appeals sitting en banc. A substantial Fund Act implementation or construction claim follows §9011(b) to a three-judge district court with direct Supreme Court appeal and no administrative-exhaustion requirement. Section 9011(a)’s thirty-day D.C. Circuit review of Commission action remains a separate route. Statutory eligibility to bring suit does not establish Article III standing on each claim.

**Authority by component:**

- National Committee of the Reform Party v. Democratic National Committee — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, “IV. The granted claims supply no basis for bypassing or requiring a different statutory tribunal”, 1999-03-17; Thomas, Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer.

**Present operation effective:** Reform Party, March 17, 1999.

title: Lemon test
current_append: Neutral eligibility, parental selection and restrictive endorsement do not cure public payment for demonstrated devotional instruction integrated into the financed educational work without reliable separation. The inquiry concerns the instructional function purchased; religious identity alone does not establish the defect, and genuinely independent private benefits, private forum access and reliably separated secular services remain distinct.
authority_append: Jackson v. Benson — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, “Parental routing does not justify the demonstrated purchase of integrated devotional instruction”, 1999-03-16; O’Connor Part I with Stone-Zsela, Stevens, Souter, Ginsburg and Breyer.
effective: Jackson v. Benson, March 16, 1999, for integrated provider-cost instructional payments; Agostini’s general inquiry retains its June 23, 1997 effective date.

fields.Open question: Jackson resolves only the demonstrated provider-cost arrangement purchasing integrated devotional instruction; it adopts no universal voucher prohibition or exclusion of religious providers and no constitutional entitlement to subsidy. Other voucher arrangements, monuments, legislative prayer, general accommodation and other aid retain their actual governing rules. Witters and Mueller remain effective for their actual private-benefit relationships.

title: Scientific expert evidence under original Rules 104(a) and 702
current_append: The reliability-and-fit duty applies to scientific, technical and other specialized knowledge under original Rule 702. Experience may supply knowledge, but a professional label does not replace a reliable connection between the method, its actual application and the proposition offered. Daubert’s nonexclusive considerations apply when useful to the particular expertise; a judge need not demand laboratory testing, publication or every consideration in every field. Abuse-of-discretion review governs both the reasonable selection of the screening method and the ultimate evidentiary ruling, while categorical legal error remains independently correctable.
authority_append: Kumho Tire Co. v. Carmichael — Canonical Decision Record, Holdings, “I. Rule 702 requires reliable specialized knowledge, whatever the field”, 1999-03-23; Breyer Parts I–II, all nine Justices. Part II, “The reliability inquiry must fit the proffer and receives abuse-of-discretion review”, supplies adaptable considerations and review of screening method.
effective: Kumho Tire, March 23, 1999, extends reliability and fit to all original Rule 702 expertise and governs selection of the inquiry; Daubert and Joiner retain their component dates.

fields.Governing question: Reliability and fit of scientific, technical and other specialized evidence under original Rules 104(a) and 702.
